title: Hit sound cue table
description: data/sound/<id>.json (V6; YOK-93): which samples play when a hit lands. The fight raises one hit cue per impact on the impact tick (source, move or special id, level, strength, outcome); every table in data/sound/ is read together and the most specific matching rule plays its thud, plus its yokai sting when it names one. Specific to general: a rule naming a move beats one naming a source beats a default (no move, no source); between rules of the same rank, the one naming more of level / strength / outcome wins, then the first (files in name order, rules in array order). Every hit must sound (V6): the tables in data/sound/ taken together need a default, a rule naming no move, source or level (or such rules naming only strength / outcome that together cover every strength and outcome); a set without one is refused and the game plays the placeholder hit pack instead, as it does when data/sound/ is empty or absent. Only data/sound/*.json is read, no subfolders. Presentation only: the sim, AI, replays and harness never read it. Authored by the animator from sound-smith's generated takes or the bought packs (AM1, AM5, AM22).

thud.description: Impact thuds; one is picked per hit from the hit's tick and attacker (no randomness), so a replay sounds the same.

sting.description: Short yokai stings layered on the thud (V6); left out = thud only.

volume_db.description: Volume of both samples in dB on the Effects bus (default 0).

offset_ticks.description: Sim ticks after the impact tick the samples start (60 per second, F3; hitstop ticks count). Default 0 = on the impact tick.

when.description: What the hit must be for this rule to match. Every field is optional; a field left out matches anything. No fields = the default rule.

move.description: A move id in data/moves/ (normal, throw or special). A special's id also matches its EX and Lv 3 versions, which fight under the same id.

source.description: The move's own source field in data/moves/ (an elder's or the Tanuki's moves keep the source of the file they come from). The validator also checks some move has it.

level.description: The special's level (A3); a normal or throw is level 1.

sample.description: A sound file under game/sound/, as a Godot path (res://sound/...). The validator checks it exists.
